title: Coefficient and terminal section transport along any scheme isomorphism
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, X,A,B schemes, σ:A≅B, h:B→X and g:A→X with σ≫h=g, and F a sheaf of Λ-modules on X [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let H be its underlying set sheaf. There exists an equivalence Γ(A,g*F)≃(h⁻¹H)(B→B). For every etale object U→X, morphism v:B→U over X and section z∈F(U), it carries the module inverse-image unit of z restricted along the graph of σ≫v and then identified with global sections to the set inverse-image unit of z restricted along the graph of v. No geometric point, strict localization or qcqs assumption is needed. Inverse images are those of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and graphs are pullback lifts [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: Construct the equivalence from global-to-terminal sections, coefficient comparison, inverse-image composition, restriction along σ, and transport of the terminal object. These are concrete isomorphisms for any σ over X.

The coefficient comparison is the adjoint transpose of the forgotten module unit. Apply the homEquiv unit identity and the inverse comparison to identify the forgotten module unit with the set unit. Naturality of this inverse comparison moves it past restriction to the terminal object.

Use the composition-unit equation for h and σ together with σ≫h=g. Naturality carries restriction to the terminal object through the inverse comparison. The pullback pasting isomorphism has the required projections.

Use the restriction comparison unit equation and naturality. After terminal-object transport, both projections of the composite restriction agree with the graph of v. Pullback extensionality identifies them. Cancel the coefficient and terminal section comparisons and evaluate at z.
